blocks.text:
Many farm owners shop for software by the monthly price. But the real question is what you lose when costs go unrecorded: a bag of urea nobody wrote down, a pakyaw crew paid twice, a harvest that looked profitable until rent and family labor came in. Good farm expense management software closes those gaps, so it pays for itself in a season or it is not worth having.

This guide sets out what to look for, where the money on a Filipino farm really goes, and how the anee.io plans compare per crop. It also says plainly what anee.io does not do.

items: **Value means cost per crop.** Solo Farmer at PHP 1,800 a year comes to about PHP 900 a crop if you plant twice a year.
**Labor is the big line.** In 2024 it took close to PHP 30,000 of the PHP 59,695 it cost to grow a hectare of palay.
**Record costs at the source.** The best tools log materials, wages and services on the task, then build the reports for you.
**Count what you do not pay in cash.** Your own labor, your land and palay given as shares are costs too.
**Check the limits.** Offline use, local payment, ads on free plans and AI credits all change the real value.

blocks.text: What makes farm expense management software good value?

A tool earns its price when it saves you from typing twice and from forgetting. So look past the feature list and ask how each cost gets in, and what comes out at the end. Here are the questions to ask, with how anee.io answers them.

blocks.text: Where does the money go on a Filipino farm?

Many expense apps focus on inputs, but inputs are the smaller share on a rice farm. In 2020, fertilizer took about 8 percent of total rice production cost. Seeds and pesticides took only 3 to 4 percent each.

Labor and land weigh far more. In 2024, labor came close to PHP 30,000 per hectare and seed to PHP 4,316, out of PHP 59,695. Land rent is also among the biggest parts of the cost of producing rice. So any farm labor management software you choose must handle crews, contracts and rent as well as fertilizer.

blocks.title: Count the costs you never paid in cash
blocks.text: Value the farmer's own labor, family and exchange labor at the going wage, and value owned land at the local rent. If you leave these out, a season can look profitable when it only paid you a small wage for your own work. Write them in, even as an estimate.

If you plant one hectare twice a year, PHP 900 a crop is about 1.5 percent of the PHP 59,695 average cost per hectare in 2024. Farm Owner fits a manager who wants a foreman or partner to enter costs from the field. Plans and limits are on the [pricing page](/pricing).
How do I run farm expenses in anee.io?

items.title: Stock the shed
items.text: Enter your fertilizer, seed and chemicals in the [farm inventory](/features/farm-inventory-and-expenses), each in its own unit and price.

items.title: Build the season
items.text: Add the tasks for each lot, with the materials and workers they need. Hired services and extra expenses go on their days too.

items.title: Tick work done
items.text: When a task is done, its stock leaves the shed and its costs flow into your expenses. Undo the tick and the stock goes back.

items.title: Record the harvest
items.text: Note yield, price and buyer in Observations after harvest, so sales sit next to costs.

items.title: Read the reports
items.text: Open the [expenses report](/features/expenses-report) and the [profit report](/features/profit-report). Then compare two seasons side by side.

blocks.text: What are the other options, and what are anee.io's limits?

A notebook and a calculator still work for a small farm. A spreadsheet adds up for you, but few farmers fill it in from the field. Free rice apps for Android can keep your rice work, expenses and harvest, then sum up what the season cost to produce and what it likely earned. General bookkeeping apps can handle the money side too, but they do not know your lots, stages or crew.

Now the limits of anee.io. It is a farm records app, not a bookkeeping system for tax filing. Libre and Libre plus Anee show a few ads, and Libre keeps one active season. Anee, the smart farm technician, needs internet and uses credits for her chats and analyses. For the cost side in detail, see our guide to the [cost of producing rice per hectare](/blog/cost-of-producing-rice-per-hectare).
Questions about farm expense management software

items.q: Is there free farm expense management software?
items.a: Yes, a spreadsheet costs nothing, and anee.io has a free Libre plan with one active season. Workers, inventory and all reports start with Solo Farmer at PHP 200 a month or PHP 1,800 a year.

items.q: Can it handle more than one farm or season?
items.a: Solo Farmer runs 3 active seasons with up to 5 lots each. Farm Owner removes those limits, so it suits several farms or many lots.

items.q: Can I see the profit of each season?
items.a: Yes. The Profit Report sets your harvest sales from Observations against everything the season cost. Compare Reports puts two seasons side by side, and Anee can explain what changed.
On Farm Owner, you can give a worker or partner a login and choose none, view or edit for each module. A diary shows every change and who made it.

items.q: How do I pay for anee.io?
items.a: You pay in pesos from any Philippine bank or wallet app. Monthly and yearly options are on the pricing page.
